newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. Sept T-bonds break out, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. Sept T-bonds break out, seen rising.

text.p: September U.S. Treasury bond futures rallied more than a full point early in Thursday's abbreviated session, staging an upside breakout that technicians said could likely presage even higher prices soon.

September T-bond futures jumped Thursday after U.S. jobs data showed tight labor conditions relaxed last month, drawing buying that hoisted the contract well above key resistance, including at 112-18/32 and June 20's four-month high at 112-24/32.
Brokers said at midmorning the contract still showed enough strength to settle above that support band, unless weak longs decided to bail out before the long weekend.

"It looks like people definitely wanted to see if once taken out, that (112-24/32) would hold," said Jim Collins, senior vice president, Smith Barney. "It looks like it's going to hold very well" and give support on any pullbacks.

"We came through that real confidently," said one bank floor broker of 112-18/32. "Anything above that level is going to be really very constructive.... This could definitely be perceived as a breakout."
"Bottom line is, if we dip it's a buying opportunity at least for the next few weeks," said Steven Poser, senior technical analyst, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"I think the real target is in the mid-114s," Poser added.
September futures then might range-trade between about 111 and 115 before targeting the mid-117 area, which would equate a drop in cash long bond yield to near 6.30 percent, he said.
A 6.0-percent cash bond yield is "not an impossibility," Poser added, although he said the further upward price path was strewn with resistance.

Afterwards, he looked for bond prices to fall again. In an daily outlook issued earlier Thursday, Poser wrote, "That means we will suck everybody into this nirvana scenario and blow them to smithereens later this summer." ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
